AWARD 1.

Vide this order I shall dispose off the 'Detailed Accident Report' (hereinafter referred to as 'DAR')
filed by the police with regard to the accident occurred on 21.05.2021 in which injured Kishore Paswan (hereinafter referred to as 'petitioner') suffered injuries.

Copy of DAR was supplied to petitioner as well as to Dalbir Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 1'), Joginder Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 2') and Bajaj Allianz General Ins. Co. Ltd. (hereinafter refereed to as 'respondent no. 3'), i.e. driver, owner and insurer of the vehicle involved in the accident i.e. car bearing registration no. DL10CT 1190 (hereinafter refereed to as 'vehicle in question').

While driving my above mentioned vehicle, I reached near Ram Murti Pasi Marg Sec-11, Rohini Delhi Adventure Sports Mall at around 7:30 PM,
then the driver of a Car XUV 500, Color- Black No. DL 10CT 1190 was driving his car at high speed, carelessly and negligently and hit my vehicle from behind with great force due to which my vehicle overturned on the road and I got injured and the driver of Car XUV 500, Color-Black No. DL 10CT 1190 also hit a pedestrian walking nearby with his car.

And after going a little distance, the above mentioned car which caused the accident stopped and when I looked back, the driver of the above mentioned car had also hit an E-rickshaw in which three persons got injured and the driver of the Car XUV 500, Color-Black No. DL 10CT 1190 got down and came to us whom I saw clearly and the people nearby caught him on the spot and I called the police and informed them about the accident and when the police arrived, I handed over the above mentioned car driver to the police"

9. My issue-wise findings are as under:-
ISSUE No.1:
Whether injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 21.05.2021 at 7.30 p.m. at Ram Murti Pasi Marg between Gate No.2 & 3, near Adventure sports Mall Sec-11, Rohini, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. car bearing registration no. DL10CT 1190 by respondent no. 1 (Dalbir Singh)?

OPP. 
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner and to prove that he has suffered injuries in this accident on account of rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A. PW1/petitioner in his evidence affidavit deposed that on 21.05.2021 at about 07.30 P.M. Ms Laxmi and her husband (injured in connected cases) were sitting in his e-rickshaw bearing no. DL-11EA-3518, as a passengers and were going to their residence Kirari, Suleman Nagar from E.S.I. Hospital Sector 15,
Rohini and he was driving the said e-rickshaw very carefully at normal speed by following all traffic rules and regulations on extreme left side of the road and when e- rickshaw reached at Rammurti Passi Marg, Sector-11 Rohini, between gate no. 2 and 3 Adventure Sports Mall, suddenly a car bearing No. DL-10CT-1190 came from back side in rash, negligent and zigzag manner with uncontrolled high speed and without following the traffic norms first hit his E-rickshaw from back side by its front left side then a green colour three wheeler goods carrier bearing no. DL-ILZ-4871 and thereafter hit a pedestrian with great impact.

PW1 further deposed that the impact was so powerful that E-rickshaw and three wheeler goods carrier both overturned and they all sustained grievous injuries He was immediately removed to Bhagwan Mahavir Kishore Paswan Vs.

In his cross examination, by Ins. Co., no suggestion put to PW1 regarding the manner in which the accident had occurred.

Nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1/petitioner, as far as negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 is concerned, as being injured petitioner is natural eye-witness of accident and respondent no. 1 has not at all cross examined the PW1.

sentences.text: being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence.

Further, there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case, meaning thereby that respondent no. 1 has nothing to say about the rash and negligence on his part and the manner in which the accident had occurred as deposed by the PW1.
Further, the DAR shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/337/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by her MLC filed along with DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.

Relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under:-
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.

Considering all this
, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered injuries in the said accident.

Accordingly, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents holding that injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 21.05.2021 at 7.30 p.m. at Ram Murti Pasi Marg between Gate No.2 & 3, near Adventure sports Mall Sec-11, Rohini, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. car bearing registration no. DL10CT 1190 by respondent no. 1.

Now, the second part of the issue in hand with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
11.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009),
held as under: -
"Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of Kishore Paswan Vs. 12. Petitioner as PW1 deposed at the time of accident he was 45 years old and used to driver e-rickshaw and earning Rs. 20,000/- per month.
He further deposed that he spent Rs.25,000/- on his medical treatment, Rs. 30,000-35,000/- each towards special diet and conveyance.
He further deposed that his wife, who was working as maid servant and earning Rs. 12,000/- per month but due to this accident she could not work and lost her earning to the tune of Rs. 72,000/-.

Whereas, in his cross examination, PW1 admitted that he has no document to show that he has incurred Rs.
25,000/- on treatment nor any document to show that he has incurred any amount towards special diet, conveyance etc. nor any document to show his income of Rs. 20,000/-.
Admittedly, the petitioner has got his treatment from the government hospital.
Therefore, in the absence of any medical bills, no amount is awarded to the petitioner towards medical expenses.

Though, there is no document except deposition of petitioner that he incurred amount on special died, conveyance etc.
but considering the long treatment record and visits to hospital, an amount of Rs. 10,000/- is awarded to the petitioner towards conveyance charges and considering the nature of injuries, it is presumed that petitioner must have taken special diet for his speedy recovery and must have spent some amount towards special diet and hence, a sum of Rs.10,000/- for special diet is granted to the petitioner.
13. Ld. counsel for petitioner has prayed that petitioner is also entitled compensation on account of loss of income during the treatment.

Though, there is no document filed by the petitioner which shows loss of income during the treatment but considering, the nature of injuries, it is presumed that petitioner could not continue his work for about one month and petitioner, being driver by profession, must have been earning Rs. 20,000/- per month.

Accordingly, Rs. 20,000/- is awarded Kishore Paswan vs Dalbir Singh And Ors on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189843722/

Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical pleas and has not filed any legal offer.

However, as stated above, one of the connected case has already been settled by the Ins. Co., which inter alia means that Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and hence, merely taking technial pleas, that too without any supporting evidence, insurnce company cannot escape from its liabilities.

In view of the above discussion, since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner /
insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.

ISSUE No.1:
Whether injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 21.05.2021 at 7.30 p.m. at Ram Murti Pasi Marg between Gate No.2 & 3, near Adventure sports Mall Sec-11, Rohini, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. car bearing registration no. DL10CT 1190 by respondent no. 1 (Dalbir Singh)?
OPP. 
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner and to prove that he has suffered injuries in this accident on account of rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A. PW1/petitioner in his evidence affidavit deposed that on 21.05.2021 at about 07.30 P.M. Ms Laxmi and her husband (injured in connected cases) were sitting in his e-rickshaw bearing no. DL-11EA-3518, as a passengers and were going to their residence Kirari, Suleman Nagar from E.S.I. Hospital Sector 15,
Rohini and he was driving the said e-rickshaw very carefully at normal speed by following all traffic rules and regulations on extreme left side of the road and when e- rickshaw reached at Rammurti Passi Marg, Sector-11 Rohini, between gate no. 2 and 3 Adventure Sports Mall, suddenly a car bearing No. DL-10CT-1190 came from back side in rash, negligent and zigzag manner with uncontrolled high speed and without following the traffic norms first hit his E-rickshaw from back side by its front left side then a green colour three wheeler goods carrier bearing no. DL-ILZ-4871 and thereafter hit a pedestrian with great impact.
Accordingly, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents holding that injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 21.05.2021 at 7.30 p.m. at Ram Murti Pasi Marg between Gate No.2 & 3, near Adventure sports Mall Sec-11, Rohini, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. car bearing registration no. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1/petitioner, as far as negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 is concerned, as being injured petitioner is natural eye-witness of accident and respondent no. 1 has not at all cross examined the PW1.
Further, respondent no. 1,

being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence.
Further, there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case, meaning thereby that respondent no. 1 has nothing to say about the rash and negligence on his part and the manner in which the accident had occurred as deposed by the PW1.
Further, the DAR shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/337/338 IPC.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered injuries in the said accident.
As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured,
petitioner is the natural eye-witness of accident and is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
Accordingly, the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
Though, there is no document except deposition of petitioner that he incurred amount on special died, conveyance etc.
but considering the long treatment record and visits to hospital, an amount of Rs. 10,000/- is awarded to the petitioner towards conveyance charges and considering the nature of injuries, it is presumed that petitioner must have taken special diet for his speedy recovery and must have spent some amount towards special diet and hence, a sum of Rs.10,000/- for special diet is granted to the petitioner.
Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical pleas and has not filed any legal offer.
